correctness.rationale: For uniformly balanced labels N=2m≥4, conditioning on S_k fixes counts in two independent uniformly permuted subwords. The internal run transitions and the boundary transition yield E[R|S_k=s]=(N+3)/2-(N-1)s²/[2k(N-k)]. The independent-copy monotonicity identity implies nonpositive covariance against any nondecreasing g(|S_k|), strict iff some weighted internal g varies; exchangeable-sign fourth moments yield Cov(R,S_k²)=-N(k-1)(N-k-1)/[(N-3)(N-1)]. Under an atomless common two-sample null, the pooled-order gaps are strictly positive and independent of labels, so W1=(1/m)sum gap|S_k| and the conditional and unconditional covariances are strictly negative. Independent exact fixed-composition enumeration m=2..5 corroborates; the proof handles arbitrary m.

value.rationale: The exact universal sign between the classical runs statistic and Wasserstein two-sample discrepancy is a useful, non-obvious dependence fact in nonparametric testing. Strict conditional covariance after observing pooled order and the general monotone additive bridge formulation provide substantially more information than one fixed quadratic discrepancy.
